newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Rain hits harvest in flood-swept Czech Republic.
newsitem.headline: Rain hits harvest in flood-swept Czech Republic.

text.p: Floods and rain are hampering the harvest in the south-eastern Czech Republic, threatening to increase losses caused by two weeks of severe flooding, the Agricultural Chamber said on Monday.
But the available harvest and reserves should still satisfy local demand over the next year and keep the market in balance, said the association's Secretary Jan Zahorka.
"Grains are ripe and should be harvested in south Moravian districts, but the soil is so saturated they (farmers) can't get to the fields," Zahorka told Reuters.
"In places where the harvest should be over it is only starting now. How much we will lose depends on the weather," he added.
Rivers were mainly falling on Monday and meteorologists forecast only showers on Monday and Tuesday, while no rains should occur on Wednesday and Thursday.

Zahorka said the floods could cut the grain harvest by about 500,000 tonnes from the June estimates of seven million tonnes. The rain, and the consequent delay in harvesting, could reduce this by a further 200,000 to 500,000.
However, he stressed that flood damage estimates were preliminary as reports have not arrived from some areas. He said that more information should be available on Thursday.
Zahorka said that domestic consumption of estimated 6.5 million tonnes would be covered as there was about 1.3 million tonnes in stock.
"It is expected that there will still be balance, though it will be a little tense, even after this damage," he said.
Zahorka said combined losses from the floods, recent rain and haze including damage to machinery, installations, crops and livestock would reach some 2.3 billion crowns.

The chamber has said that about 130,000 hectares of agricultural land has been affected by the flooding. The Agricultural Ministry said last week crops were destroyed entirely on about 50,000 hectares and damaged on 50,000 more.
He added that only "hundreds of hectares" of sugarbeet fields were hit by the floods.
The flooding swept away or damaged thousands of houses, cut road and rail links, and water and power supplies in the eastern part of the Czech Republic in the past two weeks.
Police reported 46 deaths resulting from the disaster.
